full_judgment:
Khademul Islam Chowdhury J: This Rule was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why they should not be directed to make payment of subsistence allowance to the petitioner on and from 1-12-1995 till disposal of Special Case No. 9 of 98 pending before the learned Divisional Special Judge Khulna and or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The short facts are that the petitioner joined in the service of the works programme wing of Khulna Zilla Parishad on 16-4-1982 as Upper Division Assistant, The said Work Programme wing was separated and converted into Local Government Engineering Bureau where the petitioner joined and served as Head Accountant under the Executive Engineer of the Bureau. Subsequently the petitioner was transferred to the office of the Executive Engineer respondent No. 4. The respondent No. 4 transferred the petitioner under his memo No. NI Prat/LGED/SAD/13- 18/91/2000 dated 21-7-1994 vide Annexure 'C' to the office of the respondent No. 5 but the same was not allegedly served upon him. On 8-8-1994 the petitioner took leave and during the leave respondent No. 4 released the petitioner and directed him to join in the office of the respondent No.5 vide Annexure 'D'. On an FIR lodged by the respondent No.4 Satkhira PS case No. 11 dated 10- 9-94 under sections 467, 468, 471, 109, 420 BPC was started against the petitioner for misappropriation of Taka 31,51,479 On 11-9-94 the petitioner was arrested by police. After investigation police submitted charge sheet against 13 persons including the petitioner under sections 467, 468, 471, 409, 109 read with section 5(2) Of Act II of 1947 and they were placed for trial before the Divisional Special Judge, Khulna under Special Case No.9 of 1998. The proceeding was stayed by the High Court Division on the prayer of co-accused in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 232 of 98 under section 561A CrPC and the learned Divisional Special Judge stayed further proceeding of the special case against the petitioner by order dated 1-3-1990. The High Court Division granted bail to the petitioner on 2-8-95. It is stated that since petitioner was arrested and taken into custody, petitioner was suspended from service with effect from date of his arrest by the office order dated 13-9-94 passed by respondent No. 2 according to Rule 73 BSR Part-1 vide Annexure 'H'. 

 5. The respondent Nos. 2-5 filed affidavit-in-opposition denying the material allegations. It is stated that the petitioner while serving as Accountant forged the signature of the Executive Engineer and misappropriated public money to the tune of Taka 31,51,743. Since the petitioner was arrested by police on 11-9-94 in connection with the criminal case against him he was placed under suspension on 13-9-94. The petitioner though attended office and signed attendance up to 9-11-95 and received subsistence allowance all along up to the month of November 1995, thereafter he never attended office without taking leave or permission from the authority. It is submitted that the concerned Government servant under suspension is required to give his attendance and shall not leave the place of duty without leave or prior permission of the authority. But, the petitioner abstained from attending duty and remained on unauthorised absence for long and, as such, was not entitled to get subsistence allowance under the law. It is stated that the grievance made in the Writ Petition regarding payment of subsistence grant during suspension relate to terms and conditions of the service of the petitioner within exclusive jurisdiction of the Administrative Tribunal under Article 117 of the Constitution.
